items.title: Constitution Day 2026: The moral heartbeat of the Republic
items.summary: "Constitution is not a mere lawyers' document; it is a vehicle of Life and its spirit is always the spirit of Age." — Dr Bhim Rao Ambedkar. As India celebrates Constitution Day, I look back on the deliberations of our founding fathers, who crafted a foundational charter suited for our democratic nation. What I cherish most are its guaranteed fundamental rights, an independent judiciary, checks and balances among the executive, legislature and judiciary, and an independent Election Commission. As Dr Ambedkar reminded the Assembly on November 25, 1949, if things go wrong under a Constitution, the fault lies not with the text, but with those who work it. While volumes can be written about this living document which secures justice, liberty, equality and promotes fraternity, I confine myself here to a single provision that I regard as the moral heartbeat of our Constitution: Article 21. Terse in its language, yet infinite in its interpretive potential, it states: "No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law." A Bench of Justices N Sathish Kumar and GK Muthukumaar described the litigation as an apparent ego fight between the sisters and urged them to settle their differences amicably. “ Since the entire issue appears to be only an ego fight between the sisters, viz., the 1st plaintiff and the 2nd respondent, we are of the view that the matter can be given a quietus, if the parties are really interested in resolving the dispute by arriving at an amicable settlement ,” the Court observed. items.title: Jammu and Kashmir finally gets Advocate General after two-year wait
items.summary: Senior Advocate Syed Faisal Qadri has been appointed the new Advocate General of Jammu and Kashmir. The post has remained vacant for two years. The last Advocate General, DC Raina, resigned from the post on October 18, 2024, following the formation of the Omar Abdullah-led government in Jammu and Kashmir. The long-pending vacancy had recently come under the Jammu and Kashmir High Court's scrutiny. A Public Interest Litigation (PIL) petition filed by advocate Harsh Dubey flagged concerns that the prolonged vacancy was affecting the administration of justice and statutory functions attached to the Advocate General's office. The plea also highlighted the impact on the Jammu and Kashmir Advocates’ Welfare Fund Trustee Committee, of which the Advocate General is the ex-officio chairperson. On November 5, the Jammu and Kashmir administration assured the High Court that the appointment process was underway and that the post would be filled within one month. Qadri's appointment as the new Advocate General was notified today. [Read Notification]

items.title: Community with 5% population has 40% representation in Supreme Court: Former CJI BR Gavai writes to President of India
items.summary: Former Chief Justice of India (CJI) BR Gavai has written to President of India Droupadi Murmu raising concerns that recent recommendations by the Supreme Court Collegium for the appointment or transfer of judges favour one particular community at the cost of merit, diversity and inclusivity. In a three-page letter dated November 27, Gavai questioned the functioning of the Collegium and said that recent developments warranted immediate remedial measures by all stakeholders. “Candidates belonging to one particular section of the society are being favoured for recommendation/elevation to the exclusion of everyone else including marginalized communities," the letter said. Gavai said that a particular community (left unnamed in the letter) that constitutes less than 5 per cent of the country's population has had over 40 per cent representation in the Supreme Court, and that their representation has risen manifold in the recent past. "I admit that this is not something new and that is precisely why it is increasingly becoming unforgivable," Justice Gavai expressed.
